einzeiler: Kathleen Hanna talks with rock legend Anne Wilson about her voice, career and legacy.
kurzfassung: Kathleen Hanna sits down with rock icon Anne Wilson to discuss her career, vocal evolution, and legacy with the band Heart. They explore the realities of being women in the rock industry, the creative community of the Seattle music scene, and the profound emotional power of live performance. Wilson also reflects on her upcoming documentary, In My Voice, and the defining moments of her five-decade career.
stichpunkte: Anne Wilson discusses her new documentary, In My Voice, and the surreal experience of opening up her personal life to filmmakers.
Reflecting on her early musical influences, Wilson bought Baby Love by The Supremes as her first record with her own money.
She initially sang alto in a school choir and only realized she could belt rock music in her early twenties while forming a band.
Witnessing Aretha Franklin perform live in a Los Angeles club in the 1970s deeply transformed Wilson's approach to stage freedom and emotional release.
Wilson opened her Seattle home as a safe haven for emerging grunge musicians during the local scene's rise.
She addresses the persistent, tedious nature of gender-based interview questions directed at women in rock music.
Wilson shares her rigorous vocal warmup routine, which involves singing along to entire albums to stay open and prepared.

kapitel.titel: Finding Her Voice and Musical Inspirations
The Reality of Being a Woman in Rock

clips.text: The documentary avoids a sanitized portrayal of her life by telling an authentic story that encompasses far more than just her professional accomplishments.
Witnessing a legendary singer perform up close evoked an intense, uncontrollable physical reaction that fundamentally changed her perspective on performing.
Record executives arriving in corporate attire clashed sharply with the defiant, anti-establishment ethos shared by local musicians.
Instead of performing repetitive vocal exercises, the preparation process involves singing entirely along to complete records by admired artists.
Performing a legendary song before a room full of VIPs required employing a calming mental imagery technique to manage high anxiety.

beschreibung:
Can you imagine performing with Led Zeppelin, Yo-Yo Ma, and the Obamas in the audience? Hear about the time 2013 Inductee Ann Wilson of Heart did just that on this episode of Music Makes Us. Tune in as our host, Kathleen Hanna, chats with Ann about seeing Aretha Franklin live, warming up to Elton John, the real story behind her hit song “Barracuda,” and more.
